transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I came in because... it's mostly about what happens after my shifts. I work as an attendant over at the mega-arcade and bowling alley downtown, so I'm on my feet a lot, usually working really late into the night. It gets so incredibly loud in there, you know? The bells on the games, the kids screaming, the bowling balls hitting the pins—it literally makes my ears ring for the whole drive home. 

And the drive is a total nightmare right now with all the construction on the interstate. They've had those orange cones up since, what, March? It takes me forever to get back to my place. 

But anyway, by the time I finally get out of there and deal with the traffic, I'm starving, so I’ll stop for food. The problem is I just keep going once I get home. I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then I'm rummaging through the kitchen eating chips, sweets, just... whatever’s in the apartment. And afterward, I'm honestly shocked by how much I actually ate. Which is really bad because grocery prices are insane right now. I mean, have you seen what they charge for a regular bag of chips lately? It's highway robbery.
Do you think you eat more after work because of how you're feeling, or is it just because you're hungry from not eating all day?

I mean, I am hungry, sure. But... I don't know if it's just hunger. Because once I start on those nights, it’s like... it's like I’m watching myself from the outside. I'll literally be in my head telling myself to put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is completely gone. 

And man, speaking of containers, have you noticed how incredibly cheap takeout boxes are getting lately? The place I usually hit up—this late-night diner right off the exit—they used to use those really sturdy plastic ones. You know, the black ones with the clear lids that you can wash and reuse? I used to keep a whole stack of them in my cabinets, they were great for storing bolts and screws and stuff. But now they switched to this weird cardboard material that gets completely soggy before you even park your car. It’s supposed to be eco-friendly or whatever, but it just leaks grease everywhere. I actually had to buy this heavy-duty upholstery cleaner just to get a massive stain out of my passenger seat last week. Which, by the way, do not buy the store brand of that foam cleaner. It smells exactly like wet dog when you spray it, and it took three days with the windows rolled down for the smell to finally leave my car.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating when this happens after work?

Control? I mean... no, not really. I guess that's the scariest part, it just doesn't feel like I'm the one driving, you know? It’s like a switch just gets flipped and I can't turn it off. 

Kind of like the master breakers we have in the back room at the arcade, actually. Have you ever seen the electrical setup for a place that size? It is absolutely wild. We have this one breaker panel from the late 90s that controls all the neon lights and fog machines in the laser tag arena, and the wiring is a complete rat's nest. I keep telling my manager, Gary, that it's a massive fire hazard, but he just brushes it off. 

Gary is one of those guys who thinks because he took a management seminar at a Holiday Inn ten years ago, he knows everything about everything. He makes us wear these awful, stiff polyester polo shirts that do not breathe at all. When the AC breaks—which is constantly, by the way—you're just standing behind the prize counter sweating to death while trying to count out five thousand paper tickets for some kid who wants a giant stuffed banana. I don't even know why they still use paper tickets anyway, most places went to those reloadable swipe cards years ago. It would save us so much time.
Does this feeling of not being in control happen to you in situations other than eating?

No, I don't think so. It's pretty much just with the food. I mean, I'm actually a really organized person otherwise. I like having things in order, you know? 

Like my tool collection at home. I have this pegboard system in my garage that I spent an entire weekend setting up. I outlined every single wrench and hammer with a black sharpie so I know exactly where everything goes. It's so satisfying to look at. Though, to be honest, I've been thinking about taking it all down and redoing it because I bought this new set of metric sockets from the hardware store last month. They were on clearance because the store is going out of business. 

It's really sad, actually. It's one of those old mom-and-pop hardware stores that’s been on Main Street since the 70s. The owner, Mr. Henderson, knows literally everything about plumbing. He helped me fix a leaky U-bend under my sink last year and didn't even charge me for the advice. Now there's just going to be another big box store taking over, probably selling cheap plastic tools that break after two uses. I swear, they don't make anything to last anymore. I have a blender from the 90s that could crush rocks, but my buddy bought a new one last week and the motor burned out just making a smoothie.
How do you feel about yourself after one of these eating episodes?

I feel... terrible. Just completely disgusted with myself, honestly. I look at all the wrappers and empty boxes and I just feel so ashamed. It's like, how could I let this happen again? 

Speaking of boxes and wrappers, the trash situation at my apartment complex is getting completely out of hand. They just switched management companies last month, and the new guys decided to replace the three dumpsters we had with this one massive compactor unit. The problem is, it's constantly breaking down. So you have all these people just piling their garbage bags around it, and the seagulls—man, the seagulls have figured it out. They swoop in like it's a buffet. I actually watched one of them fly off with an entire half-eaten pizza crust the other morning while I was warming up my car. My car takes forever to warm up now, by the way. I think the heater core is starting to go, which is just great because winter is basically right around the corner. I need to get it looked at, but the mechanic I usually go to just retired and moved to Florida. Can't say I blame him, though. The winters up here are brutal.
Do you think you're more likely to have one of these eating episodes when you're stressed or upset after work?

I mean, I don't really know. Maybe? I haven't really paid attention to whether I'm stressed or upset when it happens. It just kind of... happens. 

I try not to get too stressed out at work, honestly. But it's hard when you have people like Brenda from accounting constantly breathing down your neck about petty cash receipts. She sent me this passive-aggressive email last Tuesday about a $4.50 discrepancy from when I bought extra AA batteries for the laser tag vests. Like, Brenda, I'm just trying to keep the equipment running so these kids don't throw a fit when their phaser dies mid-game. Those vests go through batteries like crazy, by the way. I've been trying to convince Gary to invest in rechargeable ones, but he claims the upfront cost is too high. 

Which is ridiculous, because the math totally works out in our favor after just three months. I actually made a whole spreadsheet showing the cost analysis. I love making spreadsheets. I made one last year to track the gas mileage on my car before the heater core started acting up. It's crazy how much your MPG drops when you use the defrost setting constantly. I ended up spending way more on gas last winter than I budgeted for, which meant I had to cut back on my grocery bill. Not that it matters much with the way prices are going up everywhere. Have you seen the price of eggs lately? It's highway robbery. My neighbor started keeping chickens in her backyard just to save money, but now she has a raccoon problem. She caught one trying to pry open the coop last night. Raccoons are surprisingly smart, you know. They have those little hands that can open latches and everything.
Do you think your eating episodes are usually triggered by feeling a certain way emotionally?

I'm really not sure. I haven't noticed a specific emotion or anything like that setting it off. Like I said, it just sort of happens. 

Speaking of emotions, though, my sister called me last night practically in tears because her golden retriever, Buster, chewed through the leg of her antique coffee table. She inherited that table from our grandmother, so I get why she was upset, but honestly, Buster is just a puppy. They chew things. That's what puppies do. I told her she should have gotten him more of those rawhide bones, but she read some article online saying they're bad for dogs' digestion. So instead, she bought him these weird, expensive sweet potato chews that smell awful. 

I actually tried making sweet potato fries once in this air fryer I bought on an infomercial at 2 AM. Big mistake. They came out all soggy and limp. The guy on TV made it look so easy, but those infomercials are such a scam. I ended up returning the air fryer, which was a whole ordeal because the post office lost the tracking number. Have you ever tried dealing with the post office around the holidays? It's a nightmare. The line was out the door, and the lady in front of me was trying to ship a grandfather clock to Nebraska. A grandfather clock! Who ships a clock that big through the regular mail? You'd think you'd hire a moving company for something like that.
Do you ever feel anxious or upset right before one of these eating episodes happens?

I really haven't noticed anything like that. I don't think I'm feeling anxious or anything specific right before. It's just... I don't know, it's just not something I've paid attention to. 

Anxiety is funny, though, isn't it? Like, my cousin Mark gets terrible anxiety about flying. He actually had a panic attack on a flight to Vegas last year for a bachelor party. They almost had to turn the plane around. He said the turbulence was what set him off, but I think it was the fact that he was flying Spirit Airlines. Have you seen the legroom on those flights? It's practically non-existent. I flew them once to go see my parents in Ohio, and my knees were jammed against the seat in front of me the entire time. And they charge you for everything! You want water? That's three dollars. You want to bring a carry-on? That'll be fifty bucks. 

By the time I got to Ohio, I was so stiff I could barely walk. My dad had to come pick me up in his old pickup truck, which didn't help because the suspension on that thing is completely shot. He refuses to get it fixed because he says it gives the truck "character." He's had that truck since I was in high school. We used to load up the back with hay bales for the autumn festival the town put on every October. They had this massive corn maze that took people hours to get through. One year, some kids actually got lost in it and they had to call the fire department to help find them. Can you imagine? Getting rescued from a corn maze by guys in full turnout gear. They probably felt so embarrassed.
Do you usually feel guilty after these eating episodes are over?

I don't really know. Guilt isn't really a word I'd use, I guess. I just kind of move on with my day and don't think about it too much. 

Speaking of feeling guilty, though, I actually felt terrible last week because I accidentally jammed the main ticket redemption machine at the arcade. I was trying to refill the receipt paper, and the roll slipped out of my hand and completely jammed the internal gears. Gary was so mad. We had a line of like fifteen kids waiting to cash in their tickets for those cheap plastic spider rings and sticky hands. You know those sticky hands? The ones you throw against the wall and they just leave a weird grease mark everywhere? My mom used to absolutely hate those. She would throw them away the second my brother and I brought them home from a birthday party. 

Kids' birthday parties are so expensive nowadays, anyway. Parents rent out our whole laser tag arena for two hours and it costs an absolute fortune, plus they bring in these massive, elaborate fondant cakes that nobody actually likes eating because fondant basically tastes like sweet cardboard. I really don't understand why people don't just get regular buttercream frosting. It's a classic for a reason, you know? My aunt makes this incredible buttercream from scratch every Thanksgiving. She puts it on these pumpkin cupcakes she bakes. We usually go to her house in upstate New York for the holidays, but the drive is just brutal with all the toll booths. I really need to get one of those electronic toll passes, but I keep forgetting to order it online.
Do you think your eating episodes might be related to how you're feeling emotionally at the time they happen?

I mean, you keep asking me about my emotions, but honestly, I really couldn't tell you. I haven't noticed any connection like that. It's just eating. 

But talking about emotions again, I was watching this documentary last night about octopuses—or is it octopi? I can never remember. Anyway, it was fascinating. They were showing how these creatures can actually change color and texture based on their mood or when they're hiding from predators. They're so incredibly smart. One of them actually figured out how to unscrew a jar from the inside to get a crab that was put in there as a test. Can you believe that? A jar! 

I can barely get the lid off the salsa I buy from the grocery store. I always have to run it under hot water and bang it on the counter with a butter knife. I chipped my favorite coffee mug doing that once. It was this great mug I got at a concert when I went to see Bruce Springsteen back in, oh man, it must have been 2012. The energy at that show was just unbelievable. Three hours straight of playing, no breaks. You just don't see that kind of stamina in musicians anymore. Nowadays, they play for forty-five minutes, do one encore, and charge you two hundred bucks a ticket. It's ridiculous. Plus, the ticket fees online are almost as much as the ticket itself. I tried to buy tickets to a comedy show last month, and the "convenience fee" was thirty dollars. What's convenient about that?
Do you think your eating episodes are ever triggered by feeling overwhelmed or emotional?

I don't think so. I mean, you keep asking if I'm upset or overwhelmed, but I really just haven't noticed any kind of trigger like that. It just happens. 

Overwhelmed, though... man, that reminds me of this weekend at the arcade. We had this massive group come in for a corporate team-building event. Like fifty adults in matching polo shirts trying to play Whac-A-Mole and Skee-Ball. They were so competitive! One guy actually dove across the Skee-Ball lane to block his coworker's ball. He completely wiped out and knocked over a whole display of those giant stuffed bananas we keep behind the counter. 

Those bananas are such a pain to restock, too. They're so awkwardly shaped, and they take up half the storage room in the back. Gary ordered way too many of them last summer because he thought the Minions movie was going to make them super popular again. But nobody wants them. They all want the squishmallows. Have you seen how crazy people get over those things? We had a mom yell at me last month because we ran out of the pink axolotl one. She said it ruined her daughter's entire birthday. I mean, it's just a stuffed animal, right? But people collect them like they're gold. My niece has a whole net full of them hanging from her bedroom ceiling. It looks like a giant colorful cloud is just hovering over her bed. I helped my brother install the hooks for that net, and we couldn't find a stud in the ceiling to save our lives. We ended up having to use those heavy-duty drywall anchors. Drywall is such a terrible material anyway, if you think about it. It just crumbles if you look at it wrong.
Do you think your eating episodes have anything to do with how you're feeling emotionally at the time they happen?

I really don't. I mean, you've asked me this a few times now, and I just... I don't see a connection. It's not like I'm sitting there crying and then I start eating. It just sort of happens, you know? 

Speaking of things just happening, though, my car battery completely died on me this morning. No warning at all. I just turned the key and... nothing. Not even a click. I had to call my neighbor to give me a jump, and he came out in his bathrobe and these ridiculous fuzzy slippers that looked like bear claws. He's a nice guy, though. He works as a night security guard at that big corporate park off Route 9. He always tells me these crazy stories about the raccoons that get into the dumpsters over there. Apparently, they've figured out how to lift the heavy plastic lids by working together. Raccoons are surprisingly clever. They have those little hands that look almost human. It's kind of creepy if you think about it too much. I saw a video once where a raccoon was washing a piece of cotton candy in a puddle, and it just dissolved in his hands. He looked so heartbroken. Cotton candy is mostly air anyway, which is why it melts like that. We sell it at the arcade, but the machine is a nightmare to clean. Sugar gets spun into every little crevice, and if you don't use boiling water to scrub it out, it just turns into this rock-hard crust. Gary tried to make me clean it last week without the proper brush, and I told him it was impossible. You need the right tools for a job like that. Just like you need the right jumper cables for a car. The ones my neighbor had were super thick, heavy-duty ones. Not those cheap flimsy things you buy at the gas station.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you start during these episodes?

Yeah, it really feels like that. Once I start on those nights, it's like I'm watching myself from the outside, you know? Like I'm telling myself to put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is gone. I can't stop it. 

Containers are the worst, honestly. Especially those plastic ones you get from takeout places. They never stack right in the fridge. You always end up with a tower of them that just falls over the second you try to reach for the milk. And the lids! Don't even get me started on the lids. You put them in the dishwasher, and they warp just enough so they never fit the bottom part again. I spent like twenty minutes on Sunday trying to match lids to containers in my kitchen cabinets. It's like a puzzle where half the pieces are missing. My mom used to save every single margarine tub we ever bought. We had hundreds of them. She'd use them for leftovers, sure, but also for organizing nails in the garage, or storing buttons... she had this huge collection of vintage buttons. Some of them were made of actual bone or glass. People used to put so much craftsmanship into the smallest things back then. Now everything is just cheap plastic that breaks in a week. Like those little prizes we give out at the arcade for ten tickets. The plastic spider rings? Kids love them, but they snap in half before they even make it to the parking lot.
Do you think the eating happens because you're trying to make yourself feel better?

I don't really think so. I mean, I'm not trying to fix a bad mood or cheer myself up or anything. Like I said, it just kind of happens without me really thinking about why. 

Thinking about why people do things, though... I was watching this documentary last night about people who build those massive houses out of shipping containers. Have you seen those? It's wild. They take these giant metal boxes that have been all over the ocean and just weld them together into a living room. But the guy in the documentary was explaining how hard it is to insulate them, because metal just conducts heat and cold so easily. If you don't do it right, you basically live in an oven in the summer and a freezer in the winter. Plus, you have to cut holes in the corrugated steel for windows, which ruins the structural integrity if you don't reinforce it. My uncle tried to build a shed out of corrugated metal once. He didn't secure the roof panels right, and the first big windstorm we had, they peeled off like the lid on a tin can. One of them ended up in the neighbor's swimming pool. The neighbor was furious, obviously. He was this retired guy who spent his entire day skimming leaves out of that pool. He had one of those automatic vacuums that crawls along the bottom, but he still stood out there with the net for hours. I think it gave him something to do, you know? Retirement sounds nice in theory, but I feel like I'd get so bored just sitting around the house all day. At least at the arcade, there's always some kind of chaos happening to keep you on your toes.
Do you think eating helps you feel better after a long or stressful day at work?

I really don't think it's about feeling better after work. I mean, work is definitely stressful, but I don't come home and think, "Oh, I need to eat to unwind." It's just... I don't know, it's not a stress relief thing for me. 

Speaking of stress at work, though, Gary has been on this huge kick lately about organizing the prize counter by color instead of by ticket value. It makes zero sense. Kids come up with fifty tickets and point to a blue stuffed alien, and I have to explain that the blue section has prizes ranging from ten tickets to a thousand tickets. It's a total nightmare. I spent three hours yesterday just moving these giant neon slinkies from one shelf to another. Slinkies are so weird, right? Like, who invented a spring that walks down stairs and thought, "Yes, this is a toy." I heard it was actually an accident, like a naval engineer dropped a tension spring and watched it bounce. Kind of like how penicillin was an accident. Or microwaves! I read that a guy working on radar equipment noticed the candy bar in his pocket melted, and that's how they figured out microwaves could cook food. Which reminds me, our microwave in the breakroom at the arcade is completely busted. Someone tried to heat up a slice of pizza wrapped in aluminum foil, and it sparked like a Fourth of July sparkler. We had to unplug it, and now we all have to eat cold lunches. I've been bringing these turkey wraps, but the tortillas get all soggy by noon. You really need a good, sturdy wrap if it's going to sit in a cooler for four hours. My buddy Dave makes his own tortillas from scratch. He bought this cast-iron press and everything. Cast iron is great, but you have to season it right, otherwise everything tastes like rust.
Do you think you might be eating to distract yourself from thoughts or feelings?

I honestly haven't noticed if it's a distraction thing. I don't really sit there and think about my feelings or whatever before it happens, so I couldn't tell you if I'm trying to avoid them. 

Avoidance is a big thing with my dog, though. I have this rescue mutt, Buster, and he absolutely refuses to walk on hardwood floors. He'll stand at the edge of the living room rug and just whine until I put down a trail of towels for him to walk across to get to the kitchen. It's ridiculous. I tried buying him those little dog booties with the grips on the bottom, but he just stood there frozen like a statue for twenty minutes until I took them off. Dogs are so weird about stuff on their feet. Like when they walk in snow for the first time and do that high-stepping thing? It's hilarious. We haven't had a good snow here in years, though. I remember when I was a kid, we'd get feet of it. We'd build these massive snow forts in the front yard and stockpile snowballs. My brother was a menace with snowballs. He had this throwing arm—he actually pitched for his high school baseball team for a while. He threw out his shoulder his junior year, though, which was a huge bummer. He had to do months of physical therapy with these giant rubber resistance bands. They looked like giant rubber bands you'd use to hold a trash bag on a can, you know? Speaking of trash, the garbage trucks in my neighborhood have been coming at like 4:30 in the morning lately. The backup beep is so loud it rattles my windows. I don't know why they need to be out that early when it's pitch black.
Do you think eating helps you cope with any emotional feelings after a long day?

I don't think so. I mean, I really don't feel like I'm eating to cope with anything. It's not like I have a bad day and think, "Man, I need to go eat to deal with this." It just doesn't feel connected to my emotions like that. 

Emotions are a funny thing, though, aren't they? Like, how people get so attached to inanimate objects. My coworker, Sarah, she has this beat-up old Honda Civic that she's been driving since high school. The thing has over three hundred thousand miles on it, the AC hasn't worked since 2018, and the passenger side door doesn't open from the inside. But she refuses to get rid of it. She calls it "Betsy" and talks about it like it's a pet. I get it, though. I used to have this lucky pair of socks I wore whenever I played in this local bowling league. They were these hideous neon green argyle socks, but we won the championship the first time I wore them, so I couldn't throw them away. Bowling is a weird sport if you think about it. You're basically renting shoes that hundreds of other people have sweat in, just to throw a heavy rock at some wooden sticks. And the grease on those bowling alley pizzas? It's like a slip-and-slide on a paper plate. We used to go to this place called Pinheads, and they had this arcade section in the back. That's actually what got me into arcade maintenance in the first place. They had this vintage Pac-Man machine that was always eating quarters, and I just started tinkering with it one day. The manager was so impressed he offered me a part-time job. It's crazy how one little thing can just set the course for your whole career, you know? Like the butterfly effect or whatever.
Do you think you might be eating as a way to deal with or regulate your emotions?

I really don't. I mean, you keep asking about emotions and feelings, but I'm just not seeing a link there. I don't feel sad or mad and then start eating to fix it. It's just not how it works for me. 

Speaking of regulating things, though, the thermostat at the arcade is completely out of whack. Gary—my boss, the guy with the prize counter obsession—he locked the plastic cover over the dial because he said we were wasting electricity. So now it's constantly set to 68 degrees, which sounds fine until you realize the main floor is full of machines putting out heat, but the back office where I fix things is basically a meat locker. I have to wear a beanie indoors. Beanies are great, though. I started collecting them a few years ago. I have this one with a little propeller on top, like something out of a cartoon. I wore it to a comic convention once. Those conventions are wild, man. People spend thousands of hours making these elaborate costumes out of foam and hot glue. I saw a guy dressed as a full-size Transformer, and he could actually fold down into a car. It blew my mind. I don't know how they go to the bathroom in those things, though. That's always my first thought. Like, what happens when you've been drinking overpriced convention center soda all day and you're encased in fifty pounds of painted foam? It sounds like a logistical nightmare. Just like trying to find parking downtown on a weekend. They raised the meter rates again, and it's practically robbery now.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started eating during these episodes?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those nights, it's like... it's like I'm watching myself from the outside, you know? I'm in my head telling myself to just put the food away, stop it, but my hands just keep opening containers and wrappers until everything is completely gone. I just can't stop.

Containers are getting so hard to open these days, too. Have you noticed that? Like those hard plastic clamshell things they put electronics in. You practically need a chainsaw to get into them. I bought a new set of precision screwdrivers for the arcade the other day, and I ended up slicing my thumb open on the packaging trying to get them out. I had to go to the pharmacy to get those butterfly bandages. Pharmacies are weird places. Half the store is medicine to make you healthy, and the other half is candy and soda. It doesn't make a lot of sense. Speaking of soda, they switched the syrup at the arcade from Coke to Pepsi products last week without telling anyone, and the customers were absolutely losing their minds. People take their soda preferences very seriously. I had a guy yell at me for ten minutes because he couldn't get his Diet Coke fix. I just fix the games, man, I don't order the syrup. But people just want someone to yell at, I guess. Like when you call customer service and you finally get a real person on the phone, and you just unload on them even though it's not their fault. I try not to do that, though. I know what it's like to be on the receiving end of a rant.
Do you feel like you are unable to control what you eat during these episodes?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, it's just like I said a minute ago... I can't control what I'm eating because I can't stop my hands from grabbing it. I'm just watching myself do it, completely out of control, telling myself to stop, but I just keep eating until the food is gone. 

It's sort of like when a pinball machine goes completely haywire. You know, when the flippers just start firing on their own and the lights are flashing and you're just standing there watching the ball bounce around, totally helpless. We have this old Addams Family pinball machine—classic table, by the way, probably the best one ever made—and the main board on it is just fried. Sometimes it'll just start a multi-ball mode when no one is even playing it. Scared the life out of the night shift janitor last Tuesday. He thought the place was haunted. Honestly, this whole building is so old, it wouldn't surprise me if it was. The basement is basically a dungeon. There's this one corner down there where they keep the spare Skee-Ball wooden lanes, and it always smells like damp cardboard and old cheese. I tried to organize it once, but I found a family of raccoons living in a broken photo booth. Raccoons are incredibly smart, you know. They have these little hands that look almost human, and they can open latches and unscrew jars. I saw a video online once of a raccoon breaking into a cooler and stealing a guy's hot dogs. Just unzipped the bag and took them. People always leave their coolers unattended at the beach, which is just asking for trouble. Between the raccoons and the seagulls, you really can't turn your back on your lunch for a second.

The bells on the games, the kids screaming, the bowling balls hitting the pins—it literally makes my ears ring for the whole drive home. 

And the drive is a total nightmare right now with all the construction on the interstate. They've had those orange cones up since, what, March? It takes me forever to get back to my place. 

But anyway, by the time I finally get out of there and deal with the traffic, I'm starving, so I’ll stop for food. The problem is I just keep going once I get home. I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then I'm rummaging through the kitchen eating chips, sweets, just... whatever’s in the apartment. And afterward, I'm honestly shocked by how much I actually ate. doctor.intent: determine if the patient's excessive eating is in response to emotional states
doctor.question: Do you think you eat more after work because of how you're feeling, or is it just because you're hungry from not eating all day?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I start on those nights, it’s like I’m watching myself from the outside, telling myself to put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is gone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the motivation or feeling behind eating more after work. While they ask if it's due to feelings or hunger, the core issue related to this behavior in the profile is the loss of control during the episode, where the patient feels unable to stop eating once they start.

doctor.question: Do you feel like you are unable to control what you eat during these episodes?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I start on those nights, it’s like I’m watching myself from the outside, telling myself to put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is gone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the inability to control what is eaten during the binge episodes, which maps directly to the loss of control symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, exactly. I mean, it's just like I said a minute ago... I can't control what I'm eating because I can't stop my hands from grabbing it. I'm just watching myself do it, completely out of control, telling myself to stop, but I just keep eating until the food is gone. 

It's sort of like when a pinball machine goes completely haywire. You know, when the flippers just start firing on their own and the lights are flashing and you're just standing there watching the ball bounce around, totally helpless. We have this old Addams Family pinball machine—classic table, by the way, probably the best one ever made—and the main board on it is just fried. Sometimes it'll just start a multi-ball mode when no one is even playing it. Scared the life out of the night shift janitor last Tuesday. He thought the place was haunted. Honestly, this whole building is so old, it wouldn't surprise me if it was. The basement is basically a dungeon. There's this one corner down there where they keep the spare Skee-Ball wooden lanes, and it always smells like damp cardboard and old cheese. I tried to organize it once, but I found a family of raccoons living in a broken photo booth. Raccoons are incredibly smart, you know. They have these little hands that look almost human, and they can open latches and unscrew jars. I saw a video online once of a raccoon breaking into a cooler and stealing a guy's hot dogs. Just unzipped the bag and took them. People always leave their coolers unattended at the beach, which is just asking for trouble. Between the raccoons and the seagulls, you really can't turn your back on your lunch for a second.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's description of eating episodes, particularly the feeling of being unable to stop eating once started and the lack of control over their eating, aligns with the characteristics of Other eating disorders, specifically binge eating disorder, which is classified under F50.8 in the ICD-10.
